It relies on passive optical and infrared sensors rather than active radar for target acquisition and engagement. The system has been used to shoot down several U.S. and Israeli unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Hegseth and his senior deputy, Steve Feinberg, discussed how the DPA could be used as leverage to pressure NVIDIA’s Board of Directors to restore an executive to a company that they argued was critical to the national security of the United States. While the law provided no clear path to installing Huang back as CEO, it could be used as a warning. “Essentially they could use the DPA to force NVIDIA to shift more of its production to military projects,” said one of the three people, a member of the Trump Administration. Potentially curbing future production plans and profits of NVIDIA.
